findings.detail: The new `darkbloom sandbox setup` flow, as documented, downloads `<server>/install.sh` and runs it with `/bin/sh` as the logged-in user. The CLI checks only TLS, HTTP 200, a 1 MiB cap and a `#!` line, and the doc states it does not verify the script beyond TLS. The `--server` option accepts any https URL without credentials. This is a download-and-execute path in the same user account that holds `~/.darkbloom` (provider token, local token, add-on socket) and the provider's other local state. If the sandbox service, its CDN, a TLS-trusted intermediary, or a social-engineered `--server` value serves a malicious script, it gets user-level code execution on provider Macs. Release verification happens inside the script it would replace, so it cannot protect against a hostile script. The threat model has no boundary or threat for this installer path or the closed-source add-on. Fix: pin the script by a signature or hash checked in the CLI, or embed a signed release manifest. Restrict `--server` to an allowlist or a dev-only flag. Add a boundary entry and threat for the installer and add-on supply chain.
findings.title: Sandbox setup runs a TLS-only, unsigned install.sh as the provider user, with no matching threat-model coverage
